title: Dynamic Headroom Negotiator PRD — timebound adaptive burst & hedging
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers with reserved Dedicated pools need predictable baseline throughput but also occasional short-lived spikes. Current approaches (hard reservations, preallocated burst pools) either waste capacity or force expensive overprovisioning. We need a mechanism that safely offers timebound headroom to tenants without compromising isolation guarantees or SLAs for paying customers.

Proposal summary: Build a Dynamic Headroom Negotiator (DHN) — a control-plane + runtime policy that: (1) predicts short-term demand using lightweight signals, (2) negotiates probabilistic, timebound headroom allocations at the per-tenant level, (3) enforces latency-aware preemption hooks and graceful degradation, and (4) integrates with pricing to optionally bill for consumed headroom. DHN complements reserved pools and burst credits rather than replacing existing primitives.

Why unique: Focuses on negotiated, time-windowed headroom (e.g., 5-60s windows) that can be offered automatically or via tenant opt-in, with budgeted preemption and explicit audit trails. Emphasis on latency SLO hedging instead of raw token throughput.

Non-goals: Replacing long-term reservation contracts, real-time market-style auctions, or exposing low-level kernel scheduling knobs to customers.
acceptance_criteria: DHN can create, modify, and expire a timebound headroom lease for a tenant via API/Console (create/inspect/cancel).

During a DHN lease, tenant requests may exceed baseline reserved capacity up to negotiated headroom for the lease window; 95th percentile inference latency for other tenants on the same physical pool must not regress by more than 15% compared to baseline under comparable load.
Headroom allocations are revoked or reduced within 2s of a preemption signal when higher-priority tenants require capacity; revocation order respects tenant priority and remaining lease time.
Audit logs contain a record for each lease lifecycle event (request, grant, renewal, revocation) including reason codes and telemetry links; logs are queryable via Console for the lease ID.
A billing event is emitted for consumed headroom in alpha mode (usage-metered) and matches samples in runtime telemetry within 2% error for test traces.
Safety: No cross-tenant KV cache leakage or security boundary violations when headroom transitions occur; confirmed via penetration test checklist.
Console shows per-tenant DHN activity (active leases, recent revocations, headroom usage) and a guardrail toggle in the Dedicated settings.
Rollout plan completed: internal alpha with 2 internal customers, closed beta with 5 external tenants, GA with automated fallback policies enabled.
success_metrics: Percentage of spike events where customers received >=50% of requested headroom without manual intervention (target: 75% in beta).
Average latency delta for non-bursting tenants during DHN events (target: <=10% increase).
Number of incidents caused by DHN preemption bugs (target: 0 after beta).
Revenue uplift from optional metered headroom usage (target: measured as +3% ARR in first 6 months for participating customers).
Reduction in customer-reported overprovisioning (surveyed customers reporting lower provisioned overhead by >=20%).
implementation_notes:
Architecture: DHN consists of a control-plane service that subscribes to pool-level telemetry (queue depth, recent per-tenant QPS, token rate), a lightweight predictor (EWMA + spike detector) and a negotiator policy engine. Runtime hooks expose an API for temporary token limits per tenant instance and preemption callbacks that instruct the serving runtime to gracefully shed or migrate KV caches.

Algorithmic tradeoffs: Start with conservative heuristics (short windows, small headroom multiples) and gradually enable more aggressive prediction once we have telemetry. Use deterministic tie-breakers for revocation (priority -> remaining_lease_time -> recent_usage).

Telemetry & observability: emit lease.* metrics, headroom_granted/denied counters, preemption_events with reason tags, and per-tenant latency impact traces. Provide dashboards showing peak requests, headroom utilization, and revocation latency.

Security & compliance: All negotiations and grants recorded in audit logs; KMS-backed signing of lease tokens for Private deployments; ensure revocation tokens cannot be replayed.

Backward compatibility: DHN is opt-in per-tenant. Default behavior for existing customers remains unchanged.

Implementation milestones: 1) control-plane prototype + test harness (4w), 2) runtime preemption hook + simulator (3w), 3) console UI + API (2w), 4) internal alpha (2w), 5) beta with external tenants (4w), 6) GA hardening (3w).
open_questions: Should headroom be offered as a paid add-on by default or only as an opt-in trial?
What SLA/credits apply if DHN revocation causes a measurable latency regression for a paying tenant?
How to price sub-second bursts versus sustained bursts (e.g., 10s vs 10m) in a way that aligns incentives?
Do we allow multi-tenant pooled headroom (shared credit between team-owned tenants) or require per-tenant leases?
notes_history: 2025-02-12: Initial draft by Aisha; defined problem scope and non-goals. 2025-02-20: Architecture review with Core Runtime team — agreed to add deterministic revocation tie-breaker. 2025-02-27: Billing scoped to emit events only (no immediate billing in alpha); CFO flagged pricing complexity. 2025-03-03: Security review prelim — require signed lease tokens for Private deployments. 2025-03-05: Updated acceptance criteria to include console audit visibility and tightened revocation SLA to 2s.
